text:
ajay: Quick sync after RFC merge  we still need the minimal telemetry contract so ops/eval can detect when FP8/INT8/4-bit paths drift in output quality. What fields are required at 100% request rate vs sampled?

katie: Ops needs lightweight, always-on signals. My list: precision_profile_id, model@version, degradation_score (per-request aggregate), mean_token_confidence, batching_latency_ms, gpu_mem_pct, and prompt_fp (hashed). Keep it low-cardinality.

mike: Add kv_cache_hits and worker_queue_ms. Also want a cheap mismatch proxy: top1_token_mismatch_rate against a cached shadow.`

sophia: Per-layer dumps are expensive. Proposal: emit per-layer arrays only for sampled requests (configurable sample_rate). For all requests emit aggregates: mean_abs_delta, top_k_mismatch_rate, degradation_score. Sampled ones include per_layer_mean_abs and per_layer_max_abs.

hana: From compliance: never send raw prompts. prompt_fp is required and store a boolean prompt_present to indicate whether the prompt was redacted.

ajay: Good. We should standardize names: use snake_case and a short schema. Also include precision_profile_label (human-writable) and immutable precision_profile_id (GUID).

sophia: Draft minimal schema (string fields or numbers only):
```json
{
  "request_id": "uuid",
  "model": "redwood-medium@v1",
  "precision_profile_id": "guid-1234",
  "precision_profile_label": "fp8_headwise_fast",
  "variant": "latency-optimized",
  "degradation_score": 0.021,
  "mean_token_confidence": 0.87,
  "mean_abs_delta": 0.0015,
  "top_k_mismatch_rate": 0.004,
  "kv_cache_hits": 12,
  "batching_latency_ms": 9,
  "gpu_mem_pct": 72,
  "tokens_saved_pct": 18.2,
  "cost_delta_usd": -0.003,
  "prompt_fp": "sha256:abcd...",
  "prompt_present": "false",
  "sample_rate": "0.01"
}
```

mike: That looks fine. Now the harder bit: who controls precision switching? ops favors control-plane driven rollouts and canaries, but runtime must have a tiny safety net when control-plane unreachable (to avoid OOMs or severe tail latency).

katie: Ops: Control plane for policy/rollouts, runtime for emergency overrides. Runtime overrides must be limited to a small set of checks and require two consecutive triggers (hysteresis window) to avoid flapping.

sophia: Proposed runtime override rules: thresholds = {latency_ms: X, gpu_mem_pct: Y, degradation_score: Z}. Runtime will only downgrade precision if (A AND B) where A is infra signal (latency > X OR mem > Y) and B is quality-safe signal (degradation_score < Z) to avoid lowering precision when quality is already bad. That way runtime won't make quality worse.

ajay: Nice. Can we get a minimal FSM snippet for runbook?

sophia: FSM (pseudocode):
```
state = "NORMAL"
if infra_signal_high and quality_ok and control_plane_unreachable then
  transition -> "EMERGENCY_FALLBACK"
  apply fallback_profile
  start hysteresis_timer
if state == "EMERGENCY_FALLBACK" and (control_plane_reachable or quality_degrades) then
  if control_plane_reachable -> revert/stay per control plane
  if quality_degrades -> escalate to human-on-call
if hysteresis_timer expires and metrics stable -> revert to NORMAL via control_plane
```

hana: Please ensure runtime logs every override with reason_code and snapshot of the metrics so audits can reconstruct events.

mike: Canary strategy: start with 0.5% traffic for a new profile, shadow with high-fidelity per-layer sampling for 100% of canary requests. Monitor degradation_score and cost_delta. Auto-roll back if degradation_score median > 0.04 for 5 minutes or if top_k_mismatch_rate spike > 0.02. Human approval required to promote above 5% traffic.

ajay: Also capture `tokens_saved_pct` and `cost_delta_usd` because sometimes a tiny quality drop is acceptable for larger cost wins. The gating should be multi-dimensional.

\ksophia: (typo) I mean sophia: Agree. We'll add an evaluation hook: composite_gate = f(degradation_score, cost_delta, latency_impact) with tunable weights.

quant-bot: automated: "Follow-up recorded: telemetry schema + hybrid fallback FSM + canary gates. Action items: @sophia PR runtime override FSM, @ajay write schema yaml + examples, @mike author canary playbook, @katie retention & audit policy." :pushpin:

ajay: One more ops housekeeping: telemetry retention defaults to 30d. Enterprise customers may request longer retention after compliance review. Also scrub pii: runtime should never log prompt text.

katie: I'll add retention + access controls to ops runbook.

mike: Can we get eval to share 3-5 golden prompt families for initial calibration? @lina @maria can you help?

sophia: I'll put up the PR for the schema + FSM later today. If folks agree on the fields above I'll update the RFC appendix and we can start instrumenting a canary tomorrow.

ajay: Sounds like a plan, moving to RFC follow-up. Thanks everyone.
